post.summary: Create a field (Catalog admin widget)
post.description: 422 validation_failed lists every field problem (e.g. /choices: a choice field without choices, /type, /multiple, /maxValues, /format/<part>, /requiredAt, /show/<place>, /on, /categoryId, /categoryIds: a category that does not exist or a fourth unit field for one category, /visibility/ids: brands that do not exist or grades not in the grades list, /visibility/attributeId); 409 conflict when another field for the same category (or for every category) has the slug, or the shop already has 200 fields. Send an Idempotency-Key so a retried request makes one field. With the seo setting autoSeo on_save and Landing pages on, your AI provider writes its empty glossary title, description and FAQs when it is saved (E43), while AI copy is on and its key is in Connections; the answer has them. Without AI nothing is written: the landing_pages patterns attributeTitle and attributeDescription fill its page on every read.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key of your own per request: the same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer (Idempotent-Replayed: true); another request with it answers 409 duplicate_request.

schema.description: Unknown members are ignored.

slug.description: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes; '' (or none for a new attribute) makes a free one from the name.

type.description: Variant fields: not yes_no; unit fields: text. Type, where values live and fewer values cannot change while records have values (409 conflict).

choices.description: Required for a choice attribute: different values, each a text or { value, label } (the label defaults to the value).

unit.description: Not for yes/no and date fields.

min.description: Number fields only; at most the most.

maxValues.description: With multiple: 2 to 20 (a unit field 2, for two numbers of one unit such as a dual-SIM phone's); default the most.

format.description: null for none; the parts left out take their defaults (any characters, 1 to 200 long, no starts, no pattern, no check digit). 422 at /format/<part> for a part that is not valid.

chars.description: The characters a value may have (letters of any script).

startsWith.description: A value starts with one of these ([] = anything).

mask.description: A pattern as long as the values: A a letter, 9 a digit, * a letter or a digit, any other character itself ('' = none).

checkDigit.description: luhn: the last digit is the Luhn check digit (needs chars digits).

ignoreSpaces.description: Spaces are dropped before the check (the value is kept without them).

upperCase.description: Letters are upper-cased before the check (the value is kept that way).

requiredAt.description: Required order fields only, and then needed.

show.description: The places given change; the others keep their values (a new field: product and variant fields show on the page and in Chat, the others nowhere). 422 at /show/<place> for a place its values cannot show.

page.description: The product page shows it (variant fields: they make the options shoppers pick).

card.description: How product cards show it (variant fields: the card variants carry it).

filter.description: Shoppers can filter listings by it.

compare.description: Shown in the product comparison (product fields).

feeds.description: The feed attribute its value fills (the grade label, with feeds gradeLabel, keeps custom_label_0).

jsonLd.description: How structured data names it: as an additionalProperty, or as color, material, size or pattern (a variant field's option then names variesBy).

shopper.description: The shopper sees it on their order; an order field is also asked at checkout.

categoryId.description: A category id: this attribute is that category's definition of its slug (E45); null or '': every category. 422 at /categoryId for a category that does not exist.

categoryIds.description: Existing category ids ([] = every category); not for order and customer fields. At most 3 active unit fields apply to one category (with those above it), one of them with two values (422 at /categoryIds).

visibility.description: 'always' or null, or { when: 'brands' | 'grades', ids } (existing brand ids or grade keys, 1 to 200), or { when: 'attribute', attributeId, value } (another existing attribute).

seo.description: The glossary page; replaces it (a member left out is emptied).

delete.description: 409 conflict while records hold values of it (products and variants, units, orders or customers); 404 not_found.

post.summary: Move an order to another status of the flow (Orders admin widget)
post.description: What entering a status does depends on its role and the move's options (lists/order_flow, nextStatuses on the order): packed, shipped and delivered take serial numbers (serials, grades_serials) for the lines whose item type numbers their units: picked from units in stock (unitCapture stock) when packing, or typed (unitCapture packing) with this move or later, and every unit of a line is needed by the step its type names (unitsRequiredBefore: packed, or shipped, which also covers delivered); packed takes the dispatch video as the move's video option says; shipped needs a shipment (its tracking number unless the move's tracking is optional); delivered makes cash on delivery and pickup paid (cod.paidOnDelivery), counts units sold and credits loyalty points; cancelled gives stock, slots, offer uses and points back, cancels the open Payments payment and refunds what Payments took right after when the move's refund is auto (when Payments cannot be reached the refund stays pending in effects and is tried again; a warning says so); returned_to_origin and returned put stock back as the move's restock says (ask: send restock); refunded refunds what is left (before dispatch it acts as a cancel; with nothing paid it cancels with no money unless the move's unpaid is refuse: 409 nothing_paid); a dispatched order is never canceled or refunded as a cancel: it comes back as returned_to_origin first (money paid can be refunded meanwhile with POST /v1/orders/:id/refunds); after delivery a cancel or a refund puts the items back in stock only as the move's restock says and takes earned points back unless its points is keep. A waiting order whose method is listed in the move's paidOnConfirm is recorded as paid when moved on. 409 move_not_allowed when the flow does not list the move for staff (or the shopper paid meanwhile); 409 flow_changed when the order's role is no longer the flow's role of its status; 409 conflict when the order changed meanwhile or a refund runs at Payments for it; 422 validation_failed for a missing shipment, tracking number, serial numbers, video, note, shopperNote or restock; 503 payments_unavailable when Payments cannot be reached for a cancel; 404 not_found. A widget ticket needs the move's permission (into a refunded status orders.refund; 403 forbidden). The move is written to the history with the staff member's name (a ticket's user, or the SS-Actor-* headers of a server call, else Server), the activity log, the shopper's message and the events. Each move is one transaction: the order, its facts and everything it gives back or takes are written together, so of two moves at once one wins and the other gets 409 conflict. A move refused after it called out leaves nothing behind: a Payments payment it canceled is dropped from the order (the shopper's next pay starts a new one), and a courier booking is kept as the order's shipment and used when the move is made again (never booked twice). Send an Idempotency-Key so a retried request is done once. A move into a packed, shipped or delivered status needs the order fields required by that stage (requiredAt) first: 422 validation_failed at /fields/<id>.

post.summary: Refund part of what was paid, without a move (Orders admin widget)
post.description: Through Payments first for what Payments took (or only online, or only recorded by method), the rest recorded as given back. The part through Payments goes through the order's refund lock: it is written on the order first (an effect), only while the order's refunds are as read and no refund is pending, then sent with that effect's id as the Idempotency-Key and recorded with the rest; of two refunds at once one wins (409 conflict) and a refund Payments made is always recorded. When Payments does not answer, the refund is kept pending (refund.pending, warning refund_pending) and sent again with the same key when the order is next used. With the flow's trigger refundsCover (lists/order_flow), an order whose refunds reach what was paid moves to that refunded status when the flow lists the move. 422 validation_failed (amount above what is refundable, a missing reason, an unknown method or claimId); 409 conflict when the order changed meanwhile, or while a refund runs at Payments for it (try again in a moment); a refund its cancel left pending is not sent any more once staff refund (its effect is skipped); 502 payments_refused (nothing is recorded; the effect says failed) or 503 payments_unavailable from Payments; 404 not_found. The widget needs the orders.refund permission. Send an Idempotency-Key so a retried request is done once.

post.description: Give the variants, or the single variant's price (sku, stock …) at the top level. Photos are added afterwards (POST /v1/catalog/uploads, then POST /v1/products/:id/media). 422 validation_failed lists every field problem (for example a kind whose feature is off, an unknown category, brand, attribute, grade, location or item type, several variants without Variants; values of a part its item type does not have, each at its path: /variants and /options (variants), /variants/<n>/grade (grades), /sizeChartId (chart), /variants/<n>/parcel (parcel), /returnDays, /warrantyDays and /variants/<n>/warrantyDays (warranty), /digital/downloadLimit (downloads), /digital/licenceKeys (licenceKeys), /booking (slots), /specs/<id> and /variants/<n>/attributes/<id> (a field the type does not name)); 409 conflict when the slug or a SKU is used by another product. Send an Idempotency-Key so a retried request makes one product. With the seo setting autoSeo on_save, your AI provider writes its empty SEO title, description and FAQs when it is saved (E43), while AI copy is on and its key is in Connections (seo.source ai); the answer has them. Without AI nothing is written: the patterns fill its pages on every read. With the landing_pages settings auto on and autoCopy ai, saving it also writes one of its automatic landing pages with AI copy, kept as a landing page set to auto.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key of your own per request: the same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer (Idempotent-Replayed: true); another request with it answers 409 duplicate_request.

slug.description: Lowercase letters, digits and single dashes; '' makes one from the name. A changed slug keeps finding the product.

kind.description: digital needs Digital goods, service needs Services and bookings. Not given: the kind of the item type typeKey names, else (a new product) its category's item type's, else physical.

typeKey.description: Its item type: a key of the item_types list (an offered type, or the one it has) or a built-in type (physical, digital, service), of its kind; null or '': its first category's (or the nearest one above it), else the built-in type of its kind. While the product has units in stock its item type cannot change (409 conflict).

post.summary: Suggest product copy with your AI provider (Catalog admin widget)
post.description: Written from the product's name, brand, categories, specs and options with the AI key in Connections, in the ai_copy settings' tone, language and length unless given; nothing is saved. Needs AI copy. 422 validation_failed at /fields, /tone or /language; 404 not_found; 503 ai_not_connected; 502 ai_failed when the provider fails or gives no usable text.

post.summary: Add a file to a digital product (Catalog admin widget)
post.description: Answers a signed upload: PUT the file to upload.url with upload.headers within 15 minutes. The file is listed on the product at once (a file of the same name is replaced); a product has at most 20 files. The name is cleaned to letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore (at most 120 characters). Shoppers download the files of paid orders (GET /v1/shop/orders/{id}/downloads/{lineId}/{file}). 422 validation_failed at /name, /type, /size or /id (not a digital product, or its item type has no downloads); 404 not_found; 503 storage_not_connected. The ticket needs catalog.edit.

post.summary: Add license keys to a digital product (Catalog admin widget)
post.description: Keys are trimmed; repeats and keys the product already has are skipped. When an order is paid each unit of a digital line gets one key (each key is given once). 422 validation_failed at /keys or /id (not a digital product, or its item type has no license keys); 404 not_found. The ticket needs catalog.edit.

get.summary: Shop health: what needs fixing (Customers admin widget)
get.description: Every check runs on each read (nothing is stored): one pipeline over the products, the business.json copy, the payment methods shoppers can use now (cash on delivery while its feature is on; online payment and bank transfer when offered in the checkout setting paymentMethods and Payments is connected, bank transfer also with bankTransferVia manual; pay at pickup when offered with a pickup location), and, while Growth's token is pasted in Connections, Growth's GET /v1/settings for its tag ids.

Order lines whose unit cost was known when placed (the variant's cost). Orders count when placed in the range, in the shop's currency and not canceled. Money is minor units of the shop's currency. from must be before to, and a report covers at most 366 days; else 422 validation_failed at /from or /to. With format=csv the answer is text/csv, not JSON: the file margin.csv (the csv setting's delimiter) with the columns product_id, name, units, revenue, cost, margin; money as decimals of the shop's currency. Another format answers 422 validation_failed at /format.

post.summary: Refund a claim (again for a top-up) (Orders admin widget)
post.description: Only while the claim is approved, received or refunded (409 move_not_allowed otherwise, also when the claim changed meanwhile); the claim becomes refunded. The refund is an order refund, written on the order's refunds with the claim's id: method online (or no method on an order paid through Payments) refunds through Payments for what Payments took, the rest recorded as other; bank_transfer, cash and other are only recorded (give the money back yourself). At most refundable (see the claim). On the first refund the units count as returned on the order and, with loyalty on, points are taken back as the returns setting pointsBack says. With the flow's trigger refundsCover, an order whose refunds reach what was paid moves to that refunded status when the flow lists the move. The order's refund lock applies (see POST /v1/orders/:id/refunds): when Payments does not answer, the refund is kept pending and sent again on use. 422 validation_failed at /amount (1 to refundable; nothing paid left on the order; with method online, more than Payments took), /method (not one of the methods, or online on an order not paid through Payments), /reference or /note; 404 not_found (the claim or its order); 409 conflict when the order changed meanwhile; 502 payments_refused and 503 payments_unavailable (nothing is refunded). Send an Idempotency-Key so a retried request refunds once. The shopper gets the ecommerce.return_status message and the return.status_changed hook runs.

method.description: How the money goes back; leave it out (or null) for Payments when the order was paid through Payments, else other.

reference.description: For example the bank transfer’s reference.

note.description: Kept in the history, on the order’s refund and told to the shopper (default: the amount).

chars.description: The characters a value may have (letters of any script).

startsWith.description: A value starts with one of these ([] = anything).

mask.description: A pattern as long as the values: A a letter, 9 a digit, * a letter or a digit, any other character itself ('' = none).

checkDigit.description: luhn: the last digit is the Luhn check digit (needs chars digits).

ignoreSpaces.description: Spaces are dropped before the check (the value is kept without them).

post.summary: Import records (NDJSON, ss-import)
post.description: collection is one of size_charts, categories, brands, attributes, landings, products, serials, deals, bundles, customers, orders, loyalty, reviews, returns, alerts, wishlists; import them in that order (records must name records of an earlier step), then call finish. The body is application/x-ndjson (Content-Type), not JSON: one record per line, at most 1,000 records or 4 MB per call. Records are Ecommerce's stored shapes, every one with optional createdAt and updatedAt: size_charts { id (szc_), name, unit, columns, rows, fitAdvice, notes, active }; categories { id (cat_), slug, name, parentId, description, seo, image, sort, status, icon, content, faqs, sizeChartId, typeKey, previousSlugs }; brands { id (brd_), slug, name, description, logo, status, categoryIds, seo, sizeChartId }; attributes { id (att_), name, type, choices, unit, slug, categoryId (the category it is the definition for: one record per category, not merged by slug), categoryIds, on, multiple, visibility, card, active, seo … }; landings { id (lnd_), categoryId, brandId, grade, h1, title, description, intro, faqs, indexable }; products { id (prd_), slug, name, kind, status, … variants (var_ ids), media, sold, rating, publishedAt, previousSlugs } (a product without a variant is stored as a draft); serials { id (ser_), productId, variantId, serial, status, orderId, lineId, locationId }; deals (deal_) and bundles (bnd_) with their use count used; customers { id (cus_), userId, name, email, phone, city, blocked … }; orders { id (ord_), number, customer, address, delivery, lines, totals, promotions, payment, payments, refunds, status, history, shipment … } (money in minor units, adding up as checkout adds it); loyalty { customerId, userId, lots, history … }; reviews (rev_); returns (ret_); alerts (alr_); wishlists { userId, productIds }. Each record is found by its key: id (<prefix>_<10 to 64 of 0-9a-z>), customerId for loyalty, userId for wishlists. Each record passes Ecommerce's own check in import mode: given ids, numbers, past times and histories are kept; fields the record type does not have and values the shop derives (a category's path, a product's price or stockState …) are refused by name, as is text over a limit (never cut); slugs, SKUs, variant ids, serial numbers and landing combinations another record holds are refused. A checked record replaces the stored one (createdAt kept when it has none), so a re-run changes nothing. Nothing is sent: no message, event, alert, activity copy or IndexNow call, and no stock is held. Server token only. 404 not_found for another collection; 415 unsupported_media_type without NDJSON; 413 payload_too_large.

post.summary: Move an order to another status of the flow
post.description: What entering a status does depends on its role and the move's options (lists/order_flow, nextStatuses on the order): packed, shipped and delivered take serial numbers (serials, grades_serials) for the lines whose item type numbers their units: picked from units in stock (unitCapture stock) when packing, or typed (unitCapture packing) with this move or later, and every unit of a line is needed by the step its type names (unitsRequiredBefore: packed, or shipped, which also covers delivered); packed takes the dispatch video as the move's video option says; shipped needs a shipment (its tracking number unless the move's tracking is optional); delivered makes cash on delivery and pickup paid (cod.paidOnDelivery), counts units sold and credits loyalty points; cancelled gives stock, slots, offer uses and points back, cancels the open Payments payment and refunds what Payments took right after when the move's refund is auto (when Payments cannot be reached the refund stays pending in effects and is tried again; a warning says so); returned_to_origin and returned put stock back as the move's restock says (ask: send restock); refunded refunds what is left (before dispatch it acts as a cancel; with nothing paid it cancels with no money unless the move's unpaid is refuse: 409 nothing_paid); a dispatched order is never canceled or refunded as a cancel: it comes back as returned_to_origin first (money paid can be refunded meanwhile with POST /v1/orders/:id/refunds); after delivery a cancel or a refund puts the items back in stock only as the move's restock says and takes earned points back unless its points is keep. A waiting order whose method is listed in the move's paidOnConfirm is recorded as paid when moved on. 409 move_not_allowed when the flow does not list the move for staff (or the shopper paid meanwhile); 409 flow_changed when the order's role is no longer the flow's role of its status; 409 conflict when the order changed meanwhile or a refund runs at Payments for it; 422 validation_failed for a missing shipment, tracking number, serial numbers, video, note, shopperNote or restock; 503 payments_unavailable when Payments cannot be reached for a cancel; 404 not_found. A widget ticket needs the move's permission (into a refunded status orders.refund; 403 forbidden). The move is written to the history with the staff member's name (a ticket's user, or the SS-Actor-* headers of a server call, else Server), the activity log, the shopper's message and the events. Each move is one transaction: the order, its facts and everything it gives back or takes are written together, so of two moves at once one wins and the other gets 409 conflict. A move refused after it called out leaves nothing behind: a Payments payment it canceled is dropped from the order (the shopper's next pay starts a new one), and a courier booking is kept as the order's shipment and used when the move is made again (never booked twice). Send an Idempotency-Key so a retried request is done once. A move into a packed, shipped or delivered status needs the order fields required by that stage (requiredAt) first: 422 validation_failed at /fields/<id>.

post.description: A bank transfer, cash or another way, at most the balance due, never on a closed order (canceled, returned to origin, refunded or returned). The order's open Payments payment is canceled first so the money cannot be taken twice. With confirm, a waiting order moves on to its confirmed status in the same call. 422 validation_failed (method, amount, reference, note, confirm); 409 conflict when Payments says it was paid meanwhile or the order changed; 409 move_not_allowed when confirm finds no move to a confirmed status; 503 payments_unavailable. Send an Idempotency-Key so a retried request is done once.

parameters.description: A key of your own per request: the same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer (Idempotent-Replayed: true); another request with it answers 409 duplicate_request.

post.summary: Refund part of what was paid, without a move
post.description: Through Payments first for what Payments took (or only online, or only recorded by method), the rest recorded as given back. The part through Payments goes through the order's refund lock: it is written on the order first (an effect), only while the order's refunds are as read and no refund is pending, then sent with that effect's id as the Idempotency-Key and recorded with the rest; of two refunds at once one wins (409 conflict) and a refund Payments made is always recorded. When Payments does not answer, the refund is kept pending (refund.pending, warning refund_pending) and sent again with the same key when the order is next used. With the flow's trigger refundsCover (lists/order_flow), an order whose refunds reach what was paid moves to that refunded status when the flow lists the move. 422 validation_failed (amount above what is refundable, a missing reason, an unknown method or claimId); 409 conflict when the order changed meanwhile, or while a refund runs at Payments for it (try again in a moment); a refund its cancel left pending is not sent any more once staff refund (its effect is skipped); 502 payments_refused (nothing is recorded; the effect says failed) or 503 payments_unavailable from Payments; 404 not_found. The widget needs the orders.refund permission. Send an Idempotency-Key so a retried request is done once.

parameters.description: A key of your own per request: the same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer (Idempotent-Replayed: true); another request with it answers 409 duplicate_request.

post.summary: Create a product

Photos are added afterwards (POST /v1/catalog/uploads, then POST /v1/products/:id/media). 422 validation_failed lists every field problem (for example a kind whose feature is off, an unknown category, brand, attribute, grade, location or item type, several variants without Variants; values of a part its item type does not have, each at its path: /variants and /options (variants), /variants/<n>/grade (grades), /sizeChartId (chart), /variants/<n>/parcel (parcel), /returnDays, /warrantyDays and /variants/<n>/warrantyDays (warranty), /digital/downloadLimit (downloads), /digital/licenceKeys (licenceKeys), /booking (slots), /specs/<id> and /variants/<n>/attributes/<id> (a field the type does not name)); 409 conflict when the slug or a SKU is used by another product. Send an Idempotency-Key so a retried request makes one product. With the seo setting autoSeo on_save, your AI provider writes its empty SEO title, description and FAQs when it is saved (E43), while AI copy is on and its key is in Connections (seo.source ai); the answer has them. Without AI nothing is written: the patterns fill its pages on every read. post.summary: Mark the package received
post.description: Only while the claim is approved (409 move_not_allowed otherwise, also when the claim changed meanwhile). lines says per claimed line whether it goes back in stock: those with restock true are put back at once (each exactly once, with the products.changed hook for back-in-stock alerts), false keeps a line out of later restocks, lines not named wait for POST …/restock. 422 validation_failed at /lines (not a list), /lines/<i>/lineId (not a claimed line, or named twice), /lines/<i>/restock or /note; 404 not_found. The shopper gets the ecommerce.return_status message and the return.status_changed hook runs. A server call may name the staff member in the SS-Actor-Id and SS-Actor-Name headers: the history and notes then show their name (else Server).

note.description: Kept in the history and told to the shopper.

post.summary: Refund a claim (again for a top-up)
post.description: Only while the claim is approved, received or refunded (409 move_not_allowed otherwise, also when the claim changed meanwhile); the claim becomes refunded. The refund is an order refund, written on the order's refunds with the claim's id: method online (or no method on an order paid through Payments) refunds through Payments for what Payments took, the rest recorded as other; bank_transfer, cash and other are only recorded (give the money back yourself). At most refundable (see the claim). On the first refund the units count as returned on the order and, with loyalty on, points are taken back as the returns setting pointsBack says. With the flow's trigger refundsCover, an order whose refunds reach what was paid moves to that refunded status when the flow lists the move. The order's refund lock applies (see POST /v1/orders/:id/refunds): when Payments does not answer, the refund is kept pending and sent again on use. 422 validation_failed at /amount (1 to refundable; nothing paid left on the order; with method online, more than Payments took), /method (not one of the methods, or online on an order not paid through Payments), /reference or /note; 404 not_found (the claim or its order); 409 conflict when the order changed meanwhile; 502 payments_refused and 503 payments_unavailable (nothing is refunded). Send an Idempotency-Key so a retried request refunds once. The shopper gets the ecommerce.return_status message and the return.status_changed hook runs. A server call may name the staff member in the SS-Actor-Id and SS-Actor-Name headers: the history and notes then show their name (else Server).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key of your own per request: the same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer (Idempotent-Replayed: true); another request with it answers 409 duplicate_request.

amount.description: Minor units, at most the claim’s refundable.

method.description: How the money goes back; leave it out (or null) for Payments when the order was paid through Payments, else other.

reference.description: For example the bank transfer’s reference.

note.description: Kept in the history, on the order’s refund and told to the shopper (default: the amount).

post.summary: Reject a claim
post.description: Only while the claim is requested, approved or received (409 move_not_allowed otherwise, also when the claim changed meanwhile). The note is required: it tells the shopper why (422 validation_failed at /note). Its units can be claimed again. 404 not_found. The shopper gets the ecommerce.return_status message and the return.status_changed hook runs. A server call may name the staff member in the SS-Actor-Id and SS-Actor-Name headers: the history and notes then show their name (else Server).

note.description: Told to the shopper (required).

The shopper gets the ecommerce.return_status message and the return.status_changed hook runs. A server call may name the staff member in the SS-Actor-Id and SS-Actor-Name headers: the history and notes then show their name (else Server).

The ItemList holds the products the page shows, in its order (sort, page and limit as the grid takes them; limit defaults to the catalog setting pageSize); a list with other filters has none. post.summary: Make a return, exchange or warranty claim
post.description: Send the shopper's Accounts sign-in in the SS-Sign-In header (403 sign_in_required without a valid one). Only on the shopper's own delivered order (404 not_found; 422 not_returnable before delivery). Each line must be in its window (an exchange uses the return window) with enough units left, else 422 not_returnable with errors[0].code unknown, window_closed or quantity (also when another claim took the units at the same moment). kind is one of the returns setting kinds (default return and warranty); with the reasons setting, reason is one of those texts. photos are keys from POST /v1/shop/returns/photos, uploaded already (422 validation_failed at /photos otherwise), at most the maxPhotos setting (503 storage_not_connected). 422 validation_failed names the field (/orderId, /kind, /lines/<i>/lineId, /lines/<i>/quantity, /reason, /photos). The claim starts requested: the shopper gets the ecommerce.return_status message and the return.requested hook runs. Send an Idempotency-Key so a retried request makes one claim.

post.summary: Write a review
post.description: Send an Idempotency-Key so a retried request does not write twice. The reviews setting per decides what is reviewed. per: product (the default): the shopper signed in (SS-Sign-In) reviews productId once an order of theirs holding it was delivered; one review per product and shopper. per: order_line: the order's owner (their sign-in, or a guest's order key in SS-Order-Key) reviews one line (orderId, lineId) of a delivered order; one review per line. The review is pending, or approved at once with the reviews setting moderation: auto (it then counts in the product's rating). Errors: 403 sign_in_required (no valid sign-in; with per: order_line, neither a sign-in nor an order key); 422 validation_failed at /productId, /orderId, /lineId (also when the order has no such line), /rating, /title or /body; 404 not_found when the product is not active, or (per: order_line) the order is not theirs; 403 review_not_allowed before delivery; 409 already_reviewed.

jsonLd.description: The JSON-LD (CollectionPage with an ItemList of the products the page shows, BreadcrumbList, and a FAQPage with the seo setting faqMarkup on) as text safe to put in a script tag.

lastModified.description: The newest change of the category and of the products its first page shows: send it as your page's Last-Modified.

condition.description: Its standard condition, which structured data and feeds give its items (used when not given).

categoryId.description: The category this grade entry is the definition for (null: every category).

categoryIds.description: The categories it is for (empty: all).

category.description: The page's category (E45): the one read, else the one the attribute or grade is defined for; null for a definition for every category read without one.

title.description: Its SEO title, else its label, inside the seo setting titleTemplate.

description.description: Its SEO description, else its text, else its description, else defaultDescription.

canonical.description: The landing_pages setting gradeUrl with {key} and {category} (the page's category's slug); null without it, or when it names {category} and the page has no category.

robots.description: index, follow only with an address and text of its own (its SEO body; a page made only from patterns is thin), else noindex, follow.

jsonLd.description: The JSON-LD (DefinedTerm, and a FAQPage with the seo setting faqMarkup on) as text safe to put in a script tag.

SeoListing.description: What a listing page (a category, a landing page, or any filtered list) puts in its head and above the grid.

h1.description: The landing page's heading (an automatic one's: the setting autoTitle), else the category, brand and grade names, else the business name.

faqs.description: The landing page's FAQs, else the category's.

total.description: How many products the listing has with all its filters, counted as the grid counts them (exact up to 10,000).

status.description: The HTTP status your page answers: 404 for a filter result with no product, a filter that cannot be read (a bad price, page or sort) and a page past the end (Google asks for a 404 there, never a redirect), with robots noindex, follow; 200 otherwise — also for a category without products, a search (q) that finds nothing and a stored landing page.

landing.description: The landing page whose combination matches exactly: a stored one, else an automatic one (E43, the landing_pages setting auto) while the combination has at least autoMinProducts products and autoMinInStockVariants variants in stock; null: none.

id.description: null for an automatic page (no record).

automatic.description: An automatic landing page (E43): its heading and title from the setting autoTitle, its description from autoDescription.

jsonLd.description: The JSON-LD (CollectionPage with an ItemList of the products the page shows, BreadcrumbList, and a FAQPage with the seo setting faqMarkup on) as text safe to put in a script tag.

lastModified.description: The newest change of the category, the stored landing page and the products the page shows (when the answer names them: a category or landing page, a sorted list, or with html=1); null when none is known.

html.description: With html=1: the grid's core as plain HTML — the page's products as links with their first photo (width and height) and the price shown, and links to the previous and next pages (rel prev and next). Only escaped text and https links. Print it into the product_grid widget's place.

SeoMoved.description: The page moved (an earlier slug, or an archived product sent to its category by the catalog setting retiredUrl): answer it with a 308 to url.

slug.description: Its current slug.

url.description: Its page on your website.

SeoProduct.description: What a product page puts in its head.

title.description: The product's own SEO title as written with titleMode as_written; else titleTemplate around its own SEO title, else around the seo setting productTitle ({name}, {brand}, {category}, {storeName} and the facts {price}, {minPrice}, {maxPrice}, {options}, {inStockOptions}, {conditions}, {topSpecs}). The name in titles is never added twice.

description.description: The meta description: the product's SEO description as written (never cut), else its summary when it has 50 characters or more, else the productDescription pattern with the product's facts as they are now, else its description as text, else the seo setting defaultDescription as written. Text not written as a description is cut at a word to 160 characters.

canonical.description: The product's canonicalUrl, else its page.

image.description: The social image: its ogImage, else its first photo, else the seo setting defaultImage (null: none).

jsonLd.description: The JSON-LD as text safe to put in a script tag: a ProductGroup of the variants offered (active, priced above 0; one: a Product; none: no product node), each with its photo (else the product's), its SKU (else its feed item id), offer (the price shown after the best item deal on one unit, the higher price as a StrikethroughPrice, and for a deal that holds all day with an end validFrom and priceValidUntil), condition, return policy (the product's, its grade's or the returns setting's days, with the business.json country only: { @id } of the store-wide policy of GET /v1/seo/site when it is the store's, else its own with the return method and fees) and shipping details (physical goods: { @type: OfferShippingDetails, hasShippingService: { @id } } of the store-wide shipping policy, once it is complete), reviews, a BreadcrumbList and, with the seo setting faqMarkup on, a FAQPage.

lastModified.description: The last change of what the page shows (the product's contentUpdatedAt): send it as your page's Last-Modified.

html.description: With html=1: the product page's core as plain HTML, in the website's words and format — the breadcrumb links, the name as the page's h1, the first photo with its width and height, the price shown (or the range) with the struck-through price, availability, rating, the description (its HTML cleaned again), specs and questions. Only escaped text, https links and cleaned description HTML: no script, style or event attribute. Print it into the product_page widget's place: search engines read it before any script runs, and the widget takes the place over.

SeoSite.description: What the home page puts in its head.

title.description: The seo setting homeTitle as written, else the name in titles.

description.description: The seo setting homeDescription, else defaultDescription, as written ('' = none).

siteName.description: The site name (the seo setting brandName, else the business name): use it as og:site_name, as the structured data does.

jsonLd.description: The JSON-LD (OnlineStore or LocalBusiness with its return and shipping policies, and WebSite) as text safe to put in a script tag.

Serial.description: One unit (a numbered item) of a product variant: its serial number and, with unit fields, its values.

serial.description: Names the unit: its plain serial number (a product without unit fields: 1 to 64 letters, digits, spaces and . _ / : # -), else the first value of its first unit field that has one.

values.description: Unit field id → its values (one, or two with a field that takes two), as the field's format keeps them; {} for a plain serial number.

keys.description: serial:<serial> and <fieldId>:<value> for each value: unique across the shop's units, so no number names two units.

status.description: sold: captured on an order when it was packed (back in_stock when the order is canceled or returned).

orderId.description: The order a sold unit belongs to.

locationId.description: Where the unit is kept (Multi-location stock).

typed.description: Typed by staff when packing (serial mode typed): never was in stock; deleted when it leaves its order.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as cursor for the next page (null: the last page).

variantId.description: null: the product (any variant for back_in_stock, its lowest price for price_drop).

price.description: price_drop: the price when it was set (minor units); null for back_in_stock.

targetPrice.description: price_drop: sent once the price is at most this (minor units); null: once it is below price.

status.description: failed: its message reached no one after 5 tries.

product.description: null when the product is gone or hidden.

icon.description: A name your website maps to its icon ('' = none).

url.description: The category page (the categoryUrl setting).

count.description: Visible active products in it or below it (each once).

ShopCategory.description: A category of the tree, with the categories below it.

ShopDeal.description: A live deal as shoppers see it (no use counts, priority or rule details).

type.description: percent or fixed off, or free_delivery (no delivery fee while it covers a line of the cart).

target.description: items: off each unit of the lines it covers; cart: off those lines together (a percent of their amount, or one fixed amount spread over them). Always items for free_delivery.

value.description: percent: the percent (above 0, at most 100, decimals allowed); fixed: minor units; free_delivery: 0.

slug.description: The deal page’s address part, unique per website ('': none); shoppers open a deal by id or slug.

badgeLabel.description: A short label for product cards ('': none).

discountLabel.description: How the saving reads, for example "10% off" ('': none).

url.description: The photo’s address (null when storage is not connected).

minQuantity.description: Least units of a line (0: none).

cartTotal.description: Least the cart’s goods come to, minor units (0: none).

paymentMethods.description: Only with these payment methods ([]: any).

days.description: Weekdays it applies on, 0 = Sunday ([]: every day), in the business time zone.

timeTo.description: HH:MM it stops each day ('': midnight); before timeFrom it runs past midnight.

allowPoints.description: false: points cannot be redeemed on an order it applies to.

startsAt.description: From when it applies (inclusive); null: from now on.

endsAt.description: Until when it applies (exclusive); null: no end.

everything.description: It covers every product (the lists are empty).

price.description: Minor units.

value.description: What the balance is worth at checkout, minor units.

pending.description: Points the shopper’s orders not yet delivered will earn.

alt.description: Its text, else the product name.

ShopOrder.description: An order as its shopper sees it (never staff notes or who moved or paid it).

status.description: A status key of the website’s order flow.

statusLabel.description: The status's name for the shopper (its shopper name in the flow, else its name).

role.description: What the status means, whatever its name.

guest.description: Placed by a guest (no Accounts user).

address.description: null for pickup, digital and booking-only orders.

advance.description: The COD advance paid first (0 = none).

payUrl.description: Payments’ page while a payment waits.

fields.description: The order fields shown to the shopper with their values, as they read them; staff-only fields never show.

phone.description: E.164 when the website’s phone rules read it, else as typed.

ShopOrderLine.description: An order line at the price paid.

serials.description: The plain serial numbers of its units (units without unit field values).

unitValues.description: Per unit field shown to shoppers (show.shopper), the values of its units; unit fields not shown to shoppers never show here.

downloads.description: Digital lines of a paid order (digital_goods).

downloadsLeft.description: null: no limit (or not a paid digital line).

licenceKeys.description: Given when the order is paid.
